conviction_note: Net of four sized items: a genuinely crowded short base that mainstream screens under-report by ~10x (+2.5) and a headline organic-growth optic that will print roughly 14% against a ~10% figure the aggregators carry (+1.5), against the lock-up lapsing on the print date itself with Medtronic's exchange offer still unfiled (-2.0) and the General Counsel leaving mid-separation (-0.7); I keep the net small because the baseline's own expected move of 15.9% comes from a single observation and there is no usable option chain to trade against.

findings.finding: MMED's short interest is 5,896,696 shares at the 2026-08-14 settlement against a public float of 27.96m shares (Medtronic holds ~90% of 280.84m shares outstanding) - i.e. ~21% of float with 5.1-5.7 days to cover - yet the most widely syndicated short-interest pages display it as '2.1% of float' because they divide by shares outstanding rather than float; the position was built from 1,341,393 shares at the 2026-03-13 settlement to a 6,570,728 peak on 2026-06-30 and has been reduced only ~10% since, while the stock has roughly doubled off its 2026-05-15 low of $10.65.
findings.why_not_priced: There is no functioning listed market in which to express this: total option open interest is 833 contracts and the ATM bid-ask is 174% of mid, so the +22 vol-point 25-delta skew is a scarcity/hedging artifact in a 28m-share float rather than a statement of informed bearishness - if a real bearish consensus were priced you would also see it in the sell-side, which is 13 analysts at Strong Buy with BofA raising its target to $24 in mid-August. And the screen figure marginal holders actually read says 2.1%, not 21%, so the crowding is invisible at the point of decision.
findings.independence: stockanalysis.com computes the float-adjusted figure correctly at 21.09% of float, 5.08 days to cover, float 27.96m, same 5.90m shares - https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/mmed/statistics/ (2026-08-31). The float itself is independently established by the IPO size (28.0m shares) and Medtronic's 90.03% retained stake.

findings.finding: The IPO lock-up lapses on the morning of the print: the 424B4 is dated 2026-03-05 and EDGAR full-text search confirms it contains the phrase '180 days after the date of this prospectus' (180 days from 2026-03-05 is 2026-09-01), and that lock-up binds Medtronic's ~252.9m shares as well as every officer and director; as of 2026-08-31 Medtronic's EDGAR submissions show no S-4, no Schedule TO and no 425 has ever been filed, so the split-off exchange offer is not launched and becomes launchable from this print forward against a stated intent to finish the separation in calendar 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: The coincidence of dates is arithmetic nobody publishes: MMED reports at 3:45 a.m. PDT on the exact day the restricted period ends, and the same morning Medtronic reports and could file the S-4/TO under Rule 162 early commencement. In a split-off exchange offer the arbitrage is long parent / short subsidiary, so announcement day is mechanically negative for MMED. If this were priced you would see it in the borrow and in front-expiry put open interest, and instead total OI across the whole 2026-09-18 chain is 833 contracts. You would also see the stock discounted, and instead it sits 3.5% off its 52-week high. Coverage frames the separation as a positive de-overhang event and does not date the launch window.
findings.independence: Medtronic's own 2026-06-03 release still says 'a final decision has not been reached at this time' on structure - https://news.medtronic.com/2026-06-03-Medtronic-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-2026-results-delivers-highest-annual-revenue-growth-in-10-years - and MMED's 2026-08-21 DEF 14A adds that 'Medtronic has no obligation to pursue or consummate any further dispositions... by any specified date or at all', which widens the band in both directions. Overlaps with finding 1 only insofar as an exchange offer would give existing shorts a delivery route rather than a buy-in.

findings.finding: MiniMed's Senior VP, General Counsel and Corporate Secretary, Courtney Nelson Wills, notified the company on 2026-07-30 that she is resigning effective 2026-09-25 after an eight-week transition - disclosed in an 8-K filed 2026-08-05, i.e. she departs inside the exact window in which a tax-free split-off exchange offer, an S-4 and ~160 Medtronic transition-services agreements have to be executed.
findings.why_not_priced: An item 5.02 8-K on a non-Section-16-headline officer at a six-month-old 28m-float carve-out generates no wire coverage and no analyst note; the stock rose over the following three weeks, which is what you would expect if nobody read it. If it were priced there would be a downgrade or at least a note naming legal-execution risk on the split-off. Her own Form 4 for 2026-07-31 shows 136,384 shares held, so this is not a token role.
findings.independence: Her Form 4 of 2026-08-04 (transaction date 2026-07-31, code F, 1,762 shares withheld at $18.15) independently confirms she was still an active officer through quarter end and gives the holding size - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2062583/000211047726000004/xslF345X06/wk-form4_1785879853.xml. Otherwise independent of findings 1 and 2 except that it bears on the same separation timetable.

findings.finding: Q1 FY27 is a 14-week quarter and the two halves of the arithmetic sit in two different companies' disclosures: MiniMed's CFO said on 2026-06-03 that 'excluding the extra week, we expect Q1 growth to be roughly similar to Q4' (Q4 FY26 organic was 8.7%), while Medtronic's CFO quantified the extra selling week as '500 to 600 basis points to first-quarter growth' - stacking them implies MMED prints roughly 14% organic growth, versus the '~10% organic FY27 outlook' that quote pages and screens carry as the company's guidance.
findings.why_not_priced: The 500-600bp Q1 quantification exists only in Medtronic's guidance, never in MiniMed's; MiniMed disclosed only the 1.0-1.5% full-year effect. Nasdaq shows a single estimate for MMED and stockanalysis.com carries no quarterly estimate at all, only the FY2027 annual $3.42bn. That is the signature of a name where the headline growth number is not modelled at the quarter level, so a ~14% organic print reads as a large acceleration against a '10%' anchor to exactly the momentum and retail flow that a 28m float is most sensitive to. If this were priced there would be a published quarterly consensus above the FY run-rate and a preview note explaining the 53rd week.
findings.independence: MiniMed's CFO quote is separately reproduced by two transcript vendors - https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-6-3-mmed-stock/ and https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-minimed-sees-strong-q4-2026-growth-stock-rises-93CH-4724579 - and the 14-week quarter is corroborated by the fiscal dates themselves (FY26 ended 2026-04-24 per the 10-K, Q1 FY27 ended 2026-07-31). Partly offset by the same call's disclosure that Flex had only 'four to six weeks of selling in Q1'.

searched_and_found_nothing: Medtronic EDGAR submissions through 2026-08-24 for an S-4, Schedule TO-I/TO-C or Form 425 on the split-off: none exists, so there are no exchange-offer terms, ratio or discount to trade against yet.

FX as a revenue surprise: the Q4 FY26 gap between 15.6% reported and 8.7% organic implied ~7 points of currency, but Medtronic's 2026-06-03 FY27 guidance assumes only 'neutral to 1% accretive' FX 'based on recent rates', so the consensus revenue figure implying ~1 point of FX is consistent and there is no edge here.

A second Blackstone milestone charge in Q1 FY27: the $157m charge on MiniMed Flex hit fiscal Q4 FY26 and Medtronic stated the agreement 'is not expected to have an impact on Medtronic's results in its 2027 fiscal year' (medtechdive, 2026-03-25), which kills the recurring-charge thesis for this print.

openFDA device recall database for MiniMed recalls initiated inside the quarter (2026-04-25 to 2026-07-31): the only 2026 entry returned was a 780G software recall initiated 2026-01-30, pre-quarter and pre-dating the IPO prospectus.

openFDA MAUDE adverse-event counts by month for MINIMED-branded devices: monthly totals swing 2,597 to 7,424 with obvious batch-submission spikes, too noisy and too lagged to attribute anything to the quarter.
California WARN filings for the Northridge site: the only 2026 notice found is the 81-person February 2026 restructuring, which predates the IPO and the quarter.

MiniMed press-release newsroom and investors.minimed.com for anything undisclosed between 2026-06-23 and 2026-08-31: only the Europe Instinct launch (2026-06-23) and Flex-with-Instinct US shipping (2026-08-21), both fully in the wire.

Insulet Q2 2026 (US Omnipod +20%, US outlook cut on type-2 retention) and Tandem Q2 2026 (US sales +5%, 22,000 US pumps) for a read-through on MMED's US line: both are consistent with the US pump market MiniMed already described and neither dates a change after 2026-06-03.

Reddit / patient-forum chatter on Simplera and Instinct sensor supply or quality in the May-July window: nothing datable or attributable surfaced, only the generic 10-K risk-factor language about having 'experienced... a reduction or an interruption in supply' of Simplera.

Reconciling the FY26 'adjusted standalone EBITDA margin of 15.6%' cited on the call against a third-party 10-K summary reporting FY26 Adjusted EBITDA of $202m (~6.5% of revenue): I could not verify the $202m against the primary document, so I left this ~900bp non-GAAP bridge unsized rather than build on an unconfirmed figure.
baseline_tension: The baseline's only directional statement - a +22 vol-point 25-delta skew and a 4.59 put/call OI ratio labelled 'downside paid' - rests on 833 total contracts with an ATM spread at 174% of mid, and finding 1 argues that is hedging demand in a 28m-share float with 21% of it short rather than an informed bearish view, which cuts directly against the baseline; findings 2 and 3 lean the same way as the skew and are therefore the parts of my work most likely already in the price, while finding 4 cuts against the baseline's run-up reading by saying the number the tape sees on Tuesday morning will look like an acceleration, not a deceleration.
